program: Cash incentives for childhood vaccination in northern Nigeria

nutshell.headline: Our best estimate is $43,073 per 10 additional global QALYs.
nutshell.body: An ordinary gift supports a focused vaccination-access organization. We estimate the return from its representative core, not a special restricted offer. The gross associated-resource sensitivity is $66,332. Direct SF and Bay health benefit is zero; indirect benefit is unknown and uncredited.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: A randomized evaluation found higher vaccination coverage, and the core program is inexpensive relative to the consequences of preventable childhood disease.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The trial measured coverage, not deaths. Future disease risk, sustained survival and the additional value of a new gift require substantial judgment.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Clarify current marginal allocation after existing grants and the remaining disease risk before alternative vaccination. These uncertainties do not make the conditional estimate a measured return.

summary.label: Associated resources
summary.detail: Gross fiscal-package stress, not net societal cost; transfer-excluded proxy is $55,478.

summary.label: SF / Bay benefit
summary.detail: Nigerian beneficiaries; indirect local health is unknown and uncredited.

summary.label: Evidence
summary.detail: No mortality or QALY endpoint measured.

programSection.body: New Incentives provides caregiver cash incentives, community awareness and vaccine-stock support alongside free government vaccination in northern Nigeria.

steps.title: Make visits easier
steps.detail: Incentives help offset transport and missed income while staff verify vaccination.

steps.title: Support the existing system
steps.detail: The program also encourages demand and helps clinics address stock problems; these are one combined intervention, not separate health multipliers.

programSection.boundary: An ordinary organizational gift is represented by a 90% marginal allocation to the vaccination core. This is a prior, not an audited share or second overhead deduction. All-in core costs already include administration. Other work, including ORS and delivery experiments, receives no numerical benefit credit.

model.headline: A $10,000 gift yields an estimated 2.32164 additional QALYs.
model.body: We model 360 eligible catchment infants, not 360 completed vaccinations. The price is an analyst $25 per catchment infant; the founder’s roughly $16 per enrolled child is a different denominator. Coverage becomes health through explicit disease-risk, efficacy, additionality and finite-survival judgments.

inputs.label: Marginal vaccination-core allocation
inputs.basis: Other marginal activity remains in the gift cost; core overhead is already included.

inputs.label: Cash per eligible catchment infant
inputs.basis: All-in planning price including transfers, failures, repeat enrollment and administration; not a provider quote.

inputs.label: Extra full-course-equivalent coverage
inputs.basis: Dose/completion differences are standardized here once, with measurement and contemporary transfer. Not an empirical mortality-weighted RCT coefficient.

inputs.label: Remaining targeted-disease death risk
inputs.basis: Risk to age five among marginal not-yet-protected infants, excluding deaths before vaccination and those avoided by alternative catch-up. Not national mortality per birth.

inputs.label: Standardized-course disease efficacy
inputs.basis: Protection against that disease risk; no second incomplete-series discount.

inputs.label: Funding/output additionality
inputs.basis: Beyond existing public care, reserves and other funders. Not another trial-adherence factor.

inputs.label: Finite survival difference
inputs.best: 40 years, .99 annual survival, .85 utility, .8 persistent fraction
inputs.range: 15–60 years in joint scenarios; separate 3-year stress
inputs.basis: All life-course inputs are judgments, not observed trial follow-up. Discount is 3%.

inputs.label: Implementation and event timing
inputs.best: 2-year delay; four equally weighted event years
inputs.basis: Calendar discount is separate from discounting years after a prevented early death.

inputs.label: Other gross associated resources
inputs.basis: Public vaccine, clinic and household allowance outside NI cash. A separate proxy removes $7 transfer cash; neither is net societal cost.

model.giftHeading: How much could the estimate change?

sensitivity.headline: $2,319 / 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Joint optimistic assumptions; $3,607 with gross associated resources.

sensitivity.headline: $12.98 million / 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Lower coverage, disease risk, additionality and survival; $18.66m gross.

sensitivity.headline: $245,491 / 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Only three post-death years credited; $378,056 gross.

sensitivity.headline: No positive ratio
sensitivity.detail: Identical replacement gives zero shared benefit and harm. Clinical null with shared harm can be negative.

sensitivity.headline: Health loss remains possible
sensitivity.detail: Independent gift harm is outside funding additionality; no positive cost-effectiveness ratio is shown for negative health.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Scenarios are analyst combinations, not confidence intervals. The mortality bridge is not calibrated to an observed mortality effect. Uncredited noncore benefits and harms mean this is not a rigorous lower bound.
model.fundingBoundary: GiveWell’s March 2025 award funded nine states from January 2027 through March 2028; Niger and Yobe had separate funding. Those activities are baseline. NI’s future-plans page contains mixed-vintage, different-horizon figures that do not establish a current post-award funding gap. We use a two-year delay and 30% additionality judgment rather than count already funded children. Cash transfers are fiscal costs, not themselves consumed resources; the transfer-excluded proxy still does not resolve net public replacement or household costs.

evidence.population: Clinic catchments in three northern Nigerian states
evidence.result: Among 5,173 children aged 12–16 months across 167 clinic catchments, caregiver-reported BCG, Penta1 and measles coverage rose 16, 21 and 14 percentage points; full-series coverage rose 27 points.
evidence.transfer: The comparator retained usual services and campaigns. Self-report and selected feasible clinics limit transport. Timing effects are not added separately; the retracted incentive-size pilot was a different study.

evidence.result: Cutts et al. found a mortality benefit from PCV, supporting a causal pathway from vaccination to survival.
evidence.transfer: Different vaccine and setting; neither the 50% bundle efficacy nor Nigeria’s 3% residual disease risk is estimated by that trial.

evidence.result: The founder reports roughly $16 per enrolled child and acknowledges changing unit economics and new program experiments.
evidence.transfer: Not an independently audited marginal catchment price or proof every donated dollar creates new activity.

reservations: The model multiplies mortality-weighted coverage, disease risk and efficacy priors; which children receive extra protection remains uncertain.
Existing funding into 2028 may displace or delay a fresh gift’s effect.
Forty-year survival difference is an explicit extrapolation, not an RCT result.
A California mailing address does not make Nigerian beneficiary health local.
excludedBenefits: Nonfatal disease, adult hepatitis and neonatal outcomes outside the modeled age window.
Cash-consumption welfare, education, productivity and GiveWell moral weights.
ORS, research/innovation and other noncore benefits.
